data.narrative:
Rivan is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $47.2M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers to support a reliable peer-median analysis—no subset of three or more tightly-filtered peers could be isolated.

Given data constraints, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($47M) as a baseline proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to later-stage progression, this method implies a $94M valuation. A sensitivity band around this central estimate—accounting for reasonable variance in stage-specific step-up multiples—supports a range from $80M (low) to $109M (high).

The $94M median represents the most defensible point estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight peer comparables to validate sector-specific valuation multiples, the reliance on raised capital as a valuation proxy (which may diverge from true post-money economics), and typical Series A funding-stage volatility. A post-money valuation in the $80M–$109M range is consistent with the available data, though precision is limited by sparse public and same-stage private benchmarks in this subsector.
